clue.text: Sailor getting dampish at sea in short time

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the abbreviation for a short time

parts.note: MIN is the short form of minute, a brief time

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters of dampish are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor turns damp and queasy on a short voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor' is the definition, though 'at sea' makes the whole clue feel nautical; the anagram of DAMPISH sits inside the minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A midshipman is a junior naval officer, so a kind of sailor.

clue.text: Member of family repeating degree

indicators.note: repeating tells us to write the degree abbreviation twice over

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A relative keeps retaking the same qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeating' gives MA twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is a family member, and this is a childish word for her.

clue.text: Jazz up this quick movement

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for jazz is read from bottom to top

parts.note: trad is short for traditional jazz

explanation.surface: An instruction to liven up a fast passage of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TRAD in this down entry. 'Jazz up' looks like 'enliven', but jazz is the trad jazz of British crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move suddenly and swiftly, and a dart is such a rapid motion.

clue.text: Party in parliamentary setting getting excited

parts.note: the House is the chamber where Parliament sits
warming to something is becoming enthusiastic about it

explanation.surface: A political gathering in the chamber grows heated.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering held to celebrate moving into a new home is a type of party.

clue.text: It's good collecting second prize

indicators.note: collecting means the word for good takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: pure means virtuous, good

explanation.surface: A virtuous entrant scoops the runner-up award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' puts S inside PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is the sum of money offered as winnings in a contest, such as a boxing match.

clue.text: A seat that rider initially gets into with legs apart

indicators.note: gets into means the picked letters go inside the phrase for a seat

parts.note: a saddle is a rider's seat

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the words that and rider

explanation.surface: A horseman climbs into the saddle and sits with legs either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A seat' looks like one idea but splits as the article plus the saddle, which is cut open by the two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting astraddle means having one leg on each side, as when straddling something.

clue.text: Worthless person that rises to the top?

definitions.meaning: the froth or film of impurities that floats on a liquid's surface

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a contemptible person and the frothy layer that floats on boiling liquid.

clue.text: In the middle, stretch almost half an inch

indicators.note: In, read with 'the middle', puts the word for a stretch inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the centre is the middle
a stretch is a period of time, as in a prison term

explanation.surface: An instruction to extend something in its centre by almost half an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: An inch is about 2.54 cm, so half an inch is 1.27 cm, a little more than this metric unit: hence 'almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is about 2.54 of these metric units, so one is a little less than half an inch.

clue.text: Soup men stir, cooked before lunchtime?

indicators.note: before puts the shuffled letters ahead of the time
cooked means the letters of men stir are mixed up like ingredients

parts.note: one o'clock is a typical time for lunch

explanation.surface: Men stir a soup that is cooked before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: One o'clock as lunchtime is a crossword favourite for ONE; the question mark admits the loose timing.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup.

clue.text: Daisy is small child, one not agreeing to be kept in

indicators.note: to be kept in means the disputer goes inside the word for a small child

parts.note: a mite is a little child
an arguer is someone who disagrees

explanation.surface: A girl called Daisy is a small child who is kept in for arguing.
explanation.definitionFit: The marguerite is a type of daisy, the ox-eye daisy.

clue.text: Author forgotten before long?

definitions.meaning: anonymous, a writer whose name is unknown

explanation.definitionFit: The word means soon, and it is also short for anonymous, used for a writer whose name is unknown.

clue.text: Part of Elgar's title — nothing to be omitted from a music concert, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of a music concert are rearranged once something is taken out

parts.note: O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A note about an Elgar piece: nothing may be cut from its concert performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O ('nothing to be omitted') from the letters of A MUSIC CONCERT, then 'possibly' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's marches are called Pomp and Circumstance, so this word is part of the title.

clue.text: Officer is, without restriction, making broad statements

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word is goes round the restriction

parts.note: a tie is something that restricts or binds

explanation.surface: A senior officer is speaking freely, making sweeping claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without restriction' reads as a phrase meaning freely, but 'without' is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Generalities are vague, sweeping remarks rather than specific details.

clue.text: In work, upset about City rogue with bad little fault

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the others
upset in a down clue means the word for work is turned upside down

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
EC is the postcode of the City of London
a cad is a dishonourable man
ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: At work, someone is upset about a City rogue's minor misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the work upside down; 'In' at the start is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small sin or trivial offence.

clue.text: Bill gets so scared about entry to motorway

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

indicators.note: about here means the letters of so scared are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Bill is so nervous about joining the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SO SCARED into CESSROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A road giving entry to a place or to a main road is called this.

clue.text: Getting cross in English class, pointed and shouted

indicators.note: in puts the cross inside the abbreviations for English and class

parts.note: CL is the abbreviation for class
X is a cross
aimed means pointed at a target

explanation.surface: Someone getting angry in an English lesson points and yells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts X inside E and CL. 'cross' seems to mean angry; it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, so it means called out loudly.

clue.text: False account from traveller getting nothing right in fog

indicators.note: in places the traveller, nothing and right inside the word for fog

parts.note: mist is a thin fog
a rep is a travelling sales representative
O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A salesman lost in fog gives a false story of getting nothing right.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan shows 'fog', misread as 'log' in the text; a rep is a travelling salesperson.
explanation.definitionFit: To misreport is to give an inaccurate account, so as a noun it is a false account.

clue.text: Applaud revolutionary ruler

parts.note: Che Guevara was a famous revolutionary
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A crowd claps for a revolutionary leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to shout approval, much as one claps.

clue.text: It's best to have cold sheets

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper sheets

explanation.surface: Advice that cool bed linen is the ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, the elite.

clue.text: Second eleven at club used to maintain the creases

parts.note: a cricket or football eleven is a team
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A reserve side at a sports club keeps its kit neatly pressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests the sports club of the surface; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing appliance that puffs vapour keeps creases sharp in clothes.

clue.text: Smash to pieces, exploding inside target

indicators.note: exploding blows apart the letters of inside target so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: Something blows up inside the target, smashing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To disintegrate is to break up into fragments.

clue.text: In a circle more than one spoke

definitions.text: In a circle more than one spoke

parts.words: In a circle more than one spoke
parts.note: seems to describe several people talking in a ring, but means the straight lines from centre to rim of a circle, like a wheel's spokes, in the plural

explanation.definitionFit: These are the lines from the centre of a circle to its edge, like spokes of a wheel.

clue.text: Dress he discarded, the fool

indicators.note: discarded tells us the word he is thrown away from the word for dress

parts.note: to clothe is to dress

explanation.surface: A man throws off his outfit like an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarded' removes HE from CLOTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: Rage like a cat, heartlessly

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of the word for like a cat is removed

parts.note: a cat is furry, covered in fur

explanation.surface: Raging like a cat, with no pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the central R from FURRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is violent anger.

clue.text: Collection of money brought back this branch line

indicators.note: brought back means the word for a collection of money is read backwards

parts.note: a pool is a shared fund of money

explanation.surface: A whip-round raised the money to bring back a branch railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses POOL. A loop line is a railway branch that leaves the main line and rejoins it.
explanation.definitionFit: On railways, a loop is a short line that leaves the main line and rejoins it further on.

clue.text: Tough fabric on part of tricolour, of the highest quality

parts.note: cord is short for corduroy, a hard-wearing ribbed cloth
bleu is French for blue, one of the three colours of the French flag

explanation.surface: Hard-wearing cloth stitched onto a band of a national flag makes a superb item.
explanation.walkthrough: The tricolour is the French flag of blue, white and red, so its part is given in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means blue ribbon, a mark of top distinction, especially in cookery.

clue.text: Succeeded after taking occasional chances

indicators.note: after puts the abbreviation for succeeded behind the word for occasional

parts.note: odd means occasional, as in the odd game
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded after taking a few gambles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts S behind ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the likelihood of something happening, the betting chances.

clue.text: Knowing about missile, protesters may be acting thus

indicators.note: about means the word for knowing goes around the missile

parts.note: sly means knowing or cunning
Trident is a submarine-launched nuclear missile

explanation.surface: Anti-nuclear demonstrators, aware of a missile, may shout loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is the missile of the UK's nuclear deterrent, long a target of protest, which is why the definition fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters often chant in a harsh, loud and insistent way.
